subject: chemistry
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: What does the law of conservation of mass state about a chemical reaction?
options: The total mass of the products equals the total mass of the reactants
Mass is always lost as energy during a reaction
The mass of gas produced is always greater than the mass of solids used
Mass is created when new bonds form
questions.explain: No atoms are created or destroyed in a reaction, so the total mass of reactants and products is the same.

questions.q: What is the relative formula mass (Mr) of carbon dioxide, CO2? (Ar: C = 12, O = 16)
When a metal carbonate is heated in an open crucible, the measured mass decreases. Why?
options: A gas is produced and escapes into the surroundings
Atoms are destroyed during the reaction
The metal evaporates from the crucible
Mass is converted directly into heat energy
questions.explain: Carbon dioxide gas escapes the open container, so the mass that remains appears to fall even though total mass is conserved.

questions.q: How many moles are present in 20 g of sodium hydroxide, NaOH? (Mr = 40)
questions.explain: Moles = mass / Mr = 20 / 40 = 0.5 mol.

questions.q: What is the value of the Avogadro constant (the number of particles in one mole)?
questions.explain: One mole of any substance contains 6.02 x 10^23 particles, known as the Avogadro constant.

questions.q: What is the defining feature of an exothermic reaction?
options: Energy is transferred to the surroundings, so the temperature rises
Energy is taken in from the surroundings, so the temperature falls
questions.explain: Exothermic reactions release energy to the surroundings, causing a temperature increase.

questions.q: On a reaction profile for an exothermic reaction, how do the energy levels of the products compare with the reactants?
options: The products are at a lower energy than the reactants
The products are at a higher energy than the reactants
The products and reactants are at the same energy
The products have no measurable energy
questions.explain: In an exothermic reaction energy is released, so the products sit at a lower energy level than the reactants.

questions.q: Which of the following is an example of an endothermic process?
options: Thermal decomposition of a metal carbonate
Neutralisation of an acid by an alkali
The reaction of a metal with an acid
questions.explain: Thermal decomposition takes in energy from the surroundings, making it endothermic.

questions.q: What does the activation energy of a reaction represent?
options: The minimum energy that reacting particles must have to react
The total energy released by the reaction
The energy stored in the bonds of the products
The energy needed to cool the products
questions.explain: Activation energy is the minimum energy colliding particles need for a successful reaction.

questions.q: For H2 + Cl2 -> 2HCl, use bond energies (H-H = 436, Cl-Cl = 242, H-Cl = 431 kJ/mol) to find the overall energy change.
questions.explain: Bonds broken (436 + 242 = 678) minus bonds made (2 x 431 = 862) gives 678 - 862 = -184 kJ/mol.

questions.q: In terms of bond energies, why is a reaction overall exothermic?
options: More energy is released making bonds than is taken in breaking bonds
More energy is taken in making bonds than is released breaking bonds
No bonds are broken during the reaction
All bonds break but none reform
questions.explain: Breaking bonds is endothermic and making bonds is exothermic; if bond-making releases more energy, the reaction is exothermic overall.

questions.q: In terms of electrons, what is oxidation?
questions.explain: Oxidation is the loss of electrons (OIL RIG: Oxidation Is Loss, Reduction Is Gain).

questions.q: Which word equation correctly represents neutralisation?
questions.explain: Neutralisation of an acid by a base always produces a salt and water.

questions.q: What are the products when a reactive metal such as magnesium reacts with hydrochloric acid?
questions.explain: Metal + acid reactions produce a salt and hydrogen gas.

questions.q: On the pH scale, what pH value indicates a neutral solution?
questions.explain: A neutral solution, such as pure water, has a pH of 7.

questions.q: Which salt is produced when sulfuric acid reacts with sodium hydroxide?
questions.explain: Sulfuric acid produces sulfate salts, so it forms sodium sulfate with sodium hydroxide.

questions.q: Why must an ionic compound be molten or dissolved in water before it can be electrolysed?
options: The ions must be free to move and carry the charge
The compound must first react with oxygen
Solid ionic compounds contain no ions
questions.explain: Electrolysis needs mobile ions to carry the current; in a solid the ions are held in fixed positions.

questions.q: During electrolysis, to which electrode are the positive ions (cations) attracted?
questions.explain: Positive ions are attracted to the negatively charged cathode, where they are reduced.

questions.q: When concentrated aqueous sodium chloride solution is electrolysed, which products form at the electrodes?
options: Hydrogen at the cathode and chlorine at the anode
Sodium at the cathode and oxygen at the anode
Chlorine at the cathode and hydrogen at the anode
Oxygen at the cathode and sodium at the anode
questions.explain: Sodium is more reactive than hydrogen so hydrogen forms at the cathode, while chlorine is released at the anode from the concentrated chloride solution.

questions.q: The half equation Cu2+ + 2e- -> Cu occurs at the cathode. What type of process is this?
options: Decomposition, because a compound breaks down
questions.explain: Copper ions gain electrons at the cathode, and gaining electrons is reduction.
